property_summary: The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID only when the contract also supports interface ID ERC165; for any other interface ID, supportsInterface returns false.
The contract's supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID regardless of the result of super.supportsInterface.
The cancel function should always revert when EXECUTOR_ROLE has been granted to address(0).
For any interface ID, supportsInterface returns the same value when called before and after a cancel operation.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface returns true both before and after any cancel operation.
An operation should be cancellable only if it is pending (timestamp > _DONE_TIMESTAMP); cancel always clears the timestamp, so after cancel the operation is no longer pending.
The hasRole function returns the same value for a given role and account before and after calling cancel with the same role and account, but the mutant incorrectly flips this value after cancel.
The hasRole function must return the same value for a given role and account when called before and after a cancel operation that does not change the role membership for that account.
hasRole returns true for an account that has been granted a role, and that value is invariant under cancel operations.
Before any operation, hasRole must agree with the result of granting and revoking roles via the public interface, and cancel does not change role membership.
After a call to cancel, the timestamp of the cancelled operation is no longer pending (getTimestamp(id) == 0 or equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
After cancel(), the operation timestamp becomes non-pending, i.e., getTimestamp(id) == 0 or 1, but the buggy version reverts so it doesn't change state.
After a successful cancel, the operation's timestamp no longer shows as pending.
After cancel() returns successfully, isOperationPending() returns false and isOperationDone() returns false, meaning the operation's timestamp is exactly 0.

After a call to cancel(id) for an operation scheduled with non-zero delay completes without reverting, the operation's timestamp is no longer pending (i.e., getTimestamp(id) equals 0 or _DONE_TIMESTAMP(1)).
After scheduling an operation, cancel(bytes32) should revert if the operation is not pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After cancelling an operation, cancel(bytes32) should revert because isOperationPending returns false.
Calling cancel on an operation that was never scheduled should revert.
After scheduling an operation, cancel(bytes32) should not revert if isOperationPending returns true.
cancel should revert if isOperationPending returns false, and succeed if it returns true.
For any operation id, if it has never been scheduled (its timestamp is 0), then isOperation should return false.
If an operation id has never been scheduled, isOperation returns false.
If an operation id has not been scheduled (timestamp is 0), then before calling cancel with that id, isOperation should return false.
Cancelling a non-existing operation (timestamp is 0) should fail, but the mutant allows it.
If an operation id was never scheduled, isOperation returns false.
After cancel(bytes32 id) is called for a pending operation, the operation's timestamp is zero (isOperation returns false) regardless of any other parameters.
For any bytes32 id, the return value of isOperation(id) is equivalent to the return value of isOperationPending(id).
After a successful cancel, the operation is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After calling cancel(id) on an operation that was previously scheduled, the operation's id is no longer considered pending (isOperationPending returns false).
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel(id) on a pending operation results in isOperation(id) returning false.
For any operation id, before calling cancel(id), the operation must be pending; i.e., isOperation(id) must equal true (since isOperation returns true for pending operations).
Before cancel, isOperation() returns true for the given id.
For any operation id that is pending, isOperation returns true before cancel, and after cancel isOperation returns false.
Before cancel, isOperation returns true exactly when the operation is pending (timestamp > 0), and after cancel isOperation returns false, while cancel succeeds only if isOperation was true before.
For any id, if isOperation(id) returns false before calling cancel(id), then cancel(id) must revert.
The isOperation function returns true if and only if the operation id has a non-zero timestamp in the mapping.
Calling cancel on an operation that is not pending reverts.
Calling cancel with an id for which isOperation returns false always reverts.
Calling cancel(bytes32) on an operation that is not pending reverts.
Calling cancel on an id for which isOperation returns false always reverts.
For any id, if cancel(id) reverts, then isOperation(id) returns false.
For any id, if cancel(id) succeeds (does not revert), then isOperation(id) returns false after the cancel.
For any id, cancel(id) reverts if and only if isOperation(id) returns false before the call.
If cancel(id) does not revert, then before the call isOperation(id) must return true.
Before cancel(id) is called, isOperation(id) must return true.
For any operation id that is not pending (i.e., isOperationPending returns false), calling cancel(id) must revert.
If isOperation returns false, then calling cancel(id) must revert.
A call to cancel should revert if the operation is not pending (i.e., timestamp ≤ _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
After scheduling an operation with a delay, the operation must be ready (isOperationReady returns true) at or after the scheduled time, and the mutant incorrectly reports ready immediately.
For an operation that has never been scheduled, isOperation returns false; the mutant incorrectly returns true because it uses block.timestamp > 0.
Calling cancel on an operation that is not pending (never scheduled) reverts, refusing to allow cancellation.
For any operation id, after calling cancel(id) successfully (i.e., without revert), the operation should be marked as done (isOperationDone returns true) if the operation was previously pending.
When cancel is called on an operation that is not pending, it should revert, regardless of the operation id.
Calling cancel on a non-pending operation should revert, while cancel on a pending operation should succeed.
Calling cancel on an operation that is not pending (isOperationDone or not isOperationPending) should revert, and the return value of isOperation after a successful cancel should be false.
If isOperation returns false for a given id, then cancel(id) must revert.
If isOperation returns true for an id, then cancel(id) must succeed; if isOperation returns false, cancel(id) must revert.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) returns true if and only if the timestamp stored for that id is greater than 1.
Cancel an operation that is pending (timestamp > 1) should succeed, but canceling an operation that is not pending should revert.
Calling cancel on a pending operation should succeed, and after cancellation, isOperationPending returns false.
For any operation id, the return value of isOperationPending(id) equals the return value of getTimestamp(id) > 1.
If an operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true), then getTimestamp returns a value that is greater than 1; otherwise, isOperationPending returns false.
When an operation is pending, its timestamp is strictly greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), and when it is done, the timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
An operation canceled while pending must have had its timestamp strictly greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP before deletion.
After a successful cancel, the operation's timestamp is no longer defined (returns 0), but isOperationPending returns false because 0 is not >= 1.
After a cancel call succeeds, the operation must not be pending (isOperationPending returns false).

The cancel function should succeed (not revert) even for operations that are ready for execution (where timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP), because cancel only requires the operation to be pending, and an operation with timestamp exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP is not pending.
cancel(id) should revert when isOperationPending(id) returns false, but the buggy version returns true for operations not yet scheduled, allowing cancel to succeed incorrectly.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) must return true only if id was previously scheduled and not yet executed.
The cancel function should revert for operations that are not pending (i.e., have timestamp equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
isOperationPending returns false for any id that has never been scheduled, and calling cancel on such an id reverts.
After a successful cancel(id), isOperationPending(id) returns false.
If an operation is pending, it cannot be canceled and must have a timestamp not equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
If an operation is pending, its timestamp equals the block timestamp plus some delay, so cancel should succeed; but if cancel reverts, then isOperationPending must be false.
For any operation that is pending, cancel should succeed and after cancel the operation should not be pending.
If an operation is not pending (i.e., its timestamp is <= 1), then cancel should always revert.
For any operation that is pending (timestamp > 1), cancel should succeed and after cancellation the operation should not be pending.
For any operation that is pending, cancel should succeed and make it non-pending.
For any operation id, isOperationPending returns the same value before and after a cancel call that does not revert.
isOperationPending returns false only when the operation timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
For any operation id, cancel(id) reverts (or should revert) if and only if isOperationPending(id) returns false.
After calling cancel(id), isOperationPending(id) returns false for that id.
Before cancellation, isOperationPending must return true for a pending operation; cancel must succeed and afterwards isOperationPending must return false.
After scheduling an operation, cancel should revert if the operation is not pending.
For any operation, cancel should revert if isOperationPending returns false at the time of the call.
For any operation, isOperationPending returns true if and only if the operation has been scheduled and not yet executed or cancelled.
After scheduling an operation, before execution, cancel must revert if isOperationPending returns false.
After cancel, the operation should be done, so subsequent isOperationPending should return false.
Cancelling an operation that is pending should render it not pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After a successful cancel() call, the operation should not be pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After a scheduled operation is cancelled, isOperationPending returns false.
After cancel() is called on a pending operation, the operation is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
